- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 267-271 (_shell_segments_with_operators) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The check if segment and segment[-1].isdigit(): segment.pop() was removed before redirect tokens. When a command uses standard error redirection such as git push origin 2>/dev/null, the file descriptor digit 2 is retained in segment and parsed as a positional argument representing branch 2 rather than part of the 2> redirection operator.
  WHY: When pushing from an already-merged working branch with stderr silenced via git push origin 2>/dev/null, the guard looks up branch 2 instead of the current branch. If branch 2 has no merged pull request or does not exist, guard.evaluate() returns 0, allowing the push to proceed and stranding commits on merged history in direct violation of CLAUDE.md section 21.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 267-271 (_shell_segments_with_operators) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The template guard in workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py was changed to remove segment.pop(), while the root hook .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py still retains segment.pop().
  WHY: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:test_template_copies_are_identical asserts that TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH.read_text() == GUARD_PATH.read_text(). Because the template hook and root hook differ at lines 268-270, test_template_copies_are_identical fails in CI during the tests-hooks-and-orchestrator job.

  PROBLEM: The new test test_numeric_push_refspec_before_redirect_is_not_lost expects git push origin 2 > /dev/null to check branch 2. However, guard is imported from GUARD_PATH (.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py), which still executes segment.pop() when encountering redirection operators.
  WHY: In test_numeric_push_refspec_before_redirect_is_not_lost, segment.pop() removes 2 from the segment, causing the guard to evaluate the checked-out branch main instead of branch 2. lookups does not contain 2, and assert code == 2 fails with code == 0 in CI.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 268-269 — `if segment and segment[-1].isdigit(): segment.pop()` | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN DIFF fixed the consumer template at `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:267-270` to retain numeric push refspecs before redirects, but the in-repo root copy at `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:268-269` was not updated and still drops the trailing numeric token. The two copies now diverge.
  WHY: The new regression test `test_numeric_push_refspec_before_redirect_is_not_lost` (tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:938-954) loads `GUARD_PATH` (the root), so on `git push origin 2 > /dev/null` the root guard still pops the `2` and looks up the current branch instead of branch `2` — the test asserts `lookups == ["2"]` and `code == 2`, both of which fail. `test_template_copies_are_identical` (tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:1029-1038) also fails because `TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH.read_text()` no longer equals `GUARD_PATH.read_text()`. The CI run that produced this PR reports exactly this failure: `2 failed, 176 passed in 6.56s` in the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` job, with the failure trace showing the merge-guard code path. Reviewers in the cross-pollination pass all five flagged this same divergence with confidence 5.
- changelog.d/6055-heal-evidence-bundle.md: line 21 — "The consumer merge guard template now retains numeric push refspecs before shell redirects, preventing a push to a merged PR's numeric branch from bypassing the check. This checkout does not track the retired root `.claude/` copies; contract tests use the template assets when those copies are absent." | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN DIFF replaced an older sentence with a claim that "this checkout does not track the retired root `.claude/` copies". That claim is false for the guard and the settings file: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` and `.claude/settings.json` both exist in this checkout, are loaded by `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:30-33`, and `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` is referenced from `.claude/settings.json:81` as a real hook command. Only `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` is actually missing.
  WHY: A reader who believes the changelog will look for the root guard code in `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`, miss the divergence the prior block (and the just-removed `segment.pop()` at lines 268-269 of the root) actually document, and treat the "blocker" CI failure as a flake. The changelog is also the source of truth for `scripts/assemble_changelog.py` releases, so this inaccurate text will be folded into `CHANGELOG.md` verbatim and shipped to consumers via the `@stable` sync.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The PR description states "Review/autofix heals for pull requests in coding-workflows now target the branch the review's support scripts came from (`main` or `stable`) instead of the pull request's head branch, which had stranded the same fix twice (#4478, #4585) on branches that never reached `main`."
  Expected change site: .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (the in-repo root copy), lines 267-271.
  Evidence of absence: The LAST RUN DIFF applied the numeric-refspec retention to `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:267-270` but did not apply the matching removal of `if segment and segment[-1].isdigit(): segment.pop()` at `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:268-269`. The root copy still strips a numeric refspec adjacent to a shell redirect, so on a session that runs the root guard (the source repo's own sessions, which `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:30-31` falls back from only when the root file is missing), `git push origin 2 > /dev/null` checks the wrong branch — exactly the merge-PR bypass the LAST RUN DIFF aimed to close. The intent cannot be fully implemented until the root copy is brought into parity.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
